entries.name: mcp__linear-server__save_comment
entries.description: Create or update a comment on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. If `id` is provided, updates the existing comment; otherwise creates a new one. To start a new thread, pass `body` and exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId` (`statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent) — comments on issues/projects/initiatives become top-level discussion threads; comments on documents/milestones become description comments. A status update holds a single thread, so a comment on an update that already has one is added to it as a reply. To reply to an existing thread, pass `parentId` and `body`; the reply inherits the parent's thread type, so no entity reference is needed. Parent reference fields are ignored when `id` or `parentId` is provided (`statusUpdateType` is rejected instead).

id.description: Comment ID. If provided, updates the existing comment

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Set only together with `statusUpdateId`; omit for issue, project, initiative, document, and milestone comments. Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

parentId.description: Parent comment ID (for replies, only when creating)

body.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the returned markdown

entries.name: mcp__linear-server__save_issue
entries.description: Create or update a Linear issue. If `id` is provided, updates the existing issue; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `team` is required, and `title` is required unless `template` is set. Note: use `assignee` (not `assigneeId`) to set the assignee — it accepts a user ID, name, email, or "me".

id.description: Only for updating an existing issue. Pass the issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Do NOT pass this parameter when creating a new issue.

title.description: Issue title (required when creating, unless template is set)

description.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

patch.description: Partial edits applied to the current content, in order and atomically (one failing operation aborts the whole save). Every anchor string must match the current content exactly once. Only valid on update, in place of the full content/description field

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current content exactly once

new_string.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the match

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

anchor.description: Exact text to insert before. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly before the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")

anchor.description: Exact text to insert after. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly after the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")
Text to insert at the very start of the content
Text to insert at the very end of the content

from.description: Exact text where the range starts (inclusive). Must match exactly once

to.description: Exact text where the range ends (exclusive, stays in place). Must match exactly once after `from`

new_string.description: Text replacing the range. Empty string deletes it

team.description: Team name or ID (required when creating)

template.description: Template name or ID. Applied on create only. The template fills in the content, fields, and sub-issues server-side. A `description` replaces the template body rather than merging with it, but an empty `description` keeps the template body. Labels merge with the template's own

cycle.description: Cycle name, number, or ID. Null to remove

project.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug. Null to remove

assignee.description: User ID, name, email, or "me". Null to remove

delegate.description: Agent name or ID. When the user asks to delegate to "Linear" or "the Linear agent", this refers to the "Linear" app user specifically. Null to remove

labels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]). Replaces the full label set; existing labels not included are removed. Omit to leave labels unchanged. Cannot be combined with addLabels/removeLabels; prefer those for incremental changes

addLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to add. Append-only; existing labels are never removed. Cannot be combined with a team change

removeLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue. Cannot be combined with a team change

dueDate.description: Due date (ISO format). On update, pass null to remove the due date

slaBreachesAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the SLA will breach. On update, pass null to remove the SLA

slaType.description: SLA day counting type: "all" or "onlyBusinessDays". Only use with slaBreachesAt; null means unset

parentId.description: Parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Null to remove

estimate.description: Issue estimate value. On create, pass null or omit for no estimate. On update, pass null to clear the estimate; omitting leaves it unchanged. 0 is a real estimate only on teams that allow zero estimates.

links.description: Link attachments to add [{url, title}]. Append-only; existing links are never removed

setReleases.description: Replace all releases on the issue with these. Cannot be combined with addReleases/removeReleases

addReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to add. Append-only; existing releases are never removed

removeReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue

blocks.description: Issue IDs/identifiers this blocks. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

blockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers blocking this. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

relatedTo.description: Related issue IDs/identifiers. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

duplicateOf.description: Duplicate of issue ID/identifier. Null to remove

removeBlockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers to remove as blockers of this issue

{"id":"ENG-2061","uuid":"17320a42-9f07-49ff-bc23-ba9586e335bf","title":"Refactor `RoamFullContentNode` to use `CrossAppNode` contract","description":"## Problem

* `RoamFullContentNode` and `CrossAppNode` describe the same node. Michael: "It is basically the same type, different name" ([type](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-740e5638ca02078f61f320b8654a1a5b2cad3350046a466abd1f8bf556c95b95L11>)).
  * `RoamFullContentNode` (`convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts`) is a flat datalog row: snake_case fields, times typed `string | number`, and `text`, `format` and `node_title`.
  * `CrossAppNode` is nested, with `content.direct` and `content.full`.
* Michael: "This likely removes the need for this converter" ([converter](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-3369b2954fe17df153f37f163d9fb033a7afd3063bf9e77142aed5ff214e805aR5>)). The converter, `fullContentNodeToCrossApp` (`roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`), derives `coreTitle` from the title format and builds the full content. That work moves; it doesn't go away.

## Solution

* Remove `RoamFullContentNode`. <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>'s Done When includes this ticket.

**Open decisions**

1. Is this the first sub-ticket of <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>, part of <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>'s single change, or closed because `RoamFullContentNode` is a fair input row type?
2. Does the full-content producer, `getSharedRoamNodesWithFullContentUpdatesSince`, return `CrossAppNode` directly? <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> removed the type but deferred "Producers returning CrossAppNode directly".
3. Does this ticket also cover `RoamDiscourseNodeData` (`getAllDiscourseNodesSince.ts`), the row type the direct-content path uses? No ticket covers it.

## Done When

* `RoamFullContentNode` is gone from the Roam codebase, including tests.

## Out of Scope

* Changing the sync write calls (<issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>).

## Notes

* Current state: the type is used in `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`, `roamToCrossAppConverters.ts` and `__tests__/syncSharedNodeAssets.test.ts`. * Michael: "This likely removes the need for this converter" ([converter](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-3369b2954fe17df153f37f163d9fb033a7afd3063bf9e77142aed5ff214e805aR5>)). The converter, `fullContentNodeToCrossApp` (`roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`), derives `coreTitle` from the title format and builds the full content. That work moves; it doesn't go away.

## Solution

* Remove `RoamFullContentNode`. <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>'s Done When includes this ticket.

**Open decisions**

1. Is this the first sub-ticket of <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>, part of <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>'s single change, or closed because `RoamFullContentNode` is a fair input row type?
2. Does the full-content producer, `getSharedRoamNodesWithFullContentUpdatesSince`, return `CrossAppNode` directly? <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> removed the type but deferred "Producers returning CrossAppNode directly".
3. Does this ticket also cover `RoamDiscourseNodeData` (`getAllDiscourseNodesSince.ts`), the row type the direct-content path uses? No ticket covers it.

## Done When

* `RoamFullContentNode` is gone from the Roam codebase, including tests.

## Out of Scope

* Changing the sync write calls (<issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>).

## Notes

* Current state: the type is used in `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`, `roamToCrossAppConverters.ts` and `__tests__/syncSharedNodeAssets.test.ts`. PR <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> deletes `convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts` and types the times as `number`.
* History:
  * 2026-07-22 meeting: Marc-Antoine: "Suggestion: A converter for each roam-based type to CrossAppType, in a separate file." [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/nGZR6r8V_>) Michael: "keep all roam to cross app converters in a single file". [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Ic0cf7vkT>)
  * 2026-07-22: Marc-Antoine on <pull-request id="621db41e-f6ed-4815-aedf-03a62aeb818d" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2059-refactor-existing-roam-to-crossapp-converter-into-its-own-79ae73b79c6a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1243</pull-request>: "Rather than add a parameter to the converter, I thought I could add the full text here, as it feels natural for the type." {"id":"ENG-1824","uuid":"dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f","title":"Use the unified upsert_concepts in Roam","description":"## Problem

* Roam sync writes Concepts and Content in separate calls, to `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content`. If one call fails, we have partially defined nodes in the database.
* It would be better to send the full node, with Content as sub-objects of the Concept, in a single upsert. `upsert_concepts` accepts this since <issue id="b66b4d29-6edc-4fbe-bbbc-4cfaab6f9834" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1822/modify-upsert-concepts-so-it-accepts-embedded-content">ENG-1822</issue>.
* Roam publish already writes in a single call. Roam sync does not.

## Solution

* Remove the calls to `upsert_content`. Unify the Content computations to create the CrossAppNode type, and send it, after conversion, in a single call.

**Open decisions**

1. Does the single call go through the upsert route (<issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue>) or straight to `upsert_concepts`? On 2026-07-17 we agreed on the route. <issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue> has to confirm that still holds after v0.
2. <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue> (Roam sync onto the CrossApp converters) is the same work. Is it a step of this ticket, or does it replace this ticket? <issue id="b90793f4-5dc0-40fc-9942-95895531ba24" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2413/decide-how-roam-and-obsidian-move-onto-the-crossapp-types">ENG-2413</issue> decides this.
3. If we use the route, does this ticket also move Roam publish to it? Publish calls `upsert_concepts` directly today, and no ticket covers moving it.

## Done When

* There is no `upsert_content` call left in the Roam codebase, including test harnesses.

## Out of Scope

## Notes

* Today's `upsert_content` calls: `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts` (two calls) and `upsertNodesAsContentWithEmbeddings.ts`. Test harnesses: `fileReferenceHarness.ts` and `syncSharedNodeAssets.test.ts`.
* History:
  * 2026-05-30: Marc-Antoine created this as the Roam half of <issue id="b2336c31-b4ea-4e9a-886f-cf8e81c55e6a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1794/atomic-upsert-of-concept-and-content">ENG-1794</issue>.
  * 2026-06-25: Marc-Antoine: "Best done after <issue id="585c1ffc-4a96-443d-81a7-ced2414a7b58" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-892/add-roam-full-markdown-content-variant-for-shared-nodes">ENG-1848</issue>" (now <issue id="585c1ffc-4a96-443d-81a7-ced2414a7b58" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-892/add-roam-full-markdown-content-variant-for-shared-nodes">FEE-892</issue>).
  * 2026-07-17 meeting: agreed to change this ticket to use the upsert route. {"id":"ENG-2005","uuid":"0c10cf7e-b560-4efd-893e-bb9f5ec3a14d","title":"Zod validators for the cross-app types","description":"## Problem

We will use the cross-app types through API endpoints (see <issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2039/create-a-generic-upsert-route">ENG-2039</issue> ). These endpoints should validate the input data.

## Solution

{"id":"ENG-2165","uuid":"8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea","title":"Refactor Roam Sync to use crossAppNodes","description":"## Problem

* We have two paths to write to the database: sync and publish. They use different converters, which violates DRY.
  * Sync converts with `discourseNodeSchemaToLocalConcept`, `discourseNodeBlockToLocalConcept`, `convertRoamNodeToLocalContent` and `convertRoamNodeToFullContent`. It writes with `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content` (`syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`).
  * Publish converts with `crossAppNodeToDbConcept` and writes with `upsert_concepts` (`publishNodesToGroups.ts`).
* We want the sync to use the same CrossApp converters as publish.

## Solution

* Large-scale: Rewrite the sync to use the publish converters.
  * To be broken down in sub-tasks
* PR <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> is not code I think we should check in as-is, but Claude-generated code which I sent to help us understand the scope and surface.

**Open decisions**

1. Is this ticket a step of <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>, or does it replace <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>?
   * As a step, this ticket moves sync onto the Roam-to-CrossApp converters and keeps the current write calls. <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue> then makes the single write.
   * This answers <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>'s Open decision 2.
2. Which smaller tickets does <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> split into, and in what order? Michael asked for the split on 2026-08-28.
3. Do the items <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> deferred get their own tickets? They are `nodeTypeSince` missing child-block edits, and published isFirstChild nodes needing both a `direct_and_description` and a `direct` Content.

## Done When

* The old sync path using RoamFullContentNode is removed.
  * This will include <issue id="17320a42-9f07-49ff-bc23-ba9586e335bf" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2061/refactor-roamfullcontentnode-to-use-crossappnode-contract">ENG-2061</issue>
* The sync path only upserts Concepts, with embedded Content, vs the two phases we have now.
  * <issue id="b2336c31-b4ea-4e9a-886f-cf8e81c55e6a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1794/atomic-upsert-of-concept-and-content">ENG-1794</issue>
  * <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue> has the same Done When. Open decision 1 decides which ticket owns it.

## Out of Scope

* Moving Roam publish to the upsert route. <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>'s Open decision 3 covers it.

## Notes

* Current state:
  * PR <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> is a draft. It conflicts with main and was last updated on 2026-08-23.
  * If the upsert route stays the goal (<issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue>), sync only converts Roam data to CrossApp types, and the route converts them to database rows.
  * The sync schema converter now writes `template_content` (`conceptConversion.ts`), so the "template key" problem in the investigation below looks fixed on main.
* We still need to handle the discrepancy between direct and direct_and_description
  * Separate task but describing here
  * Published nodes with isFirst child need both to be maintained by sync
    * In sync, we can put the direct_and_description variant in the direct field of the Content (for isFirstChild nodes)
    * And send the direct variant of published, isFirstChild nodes at sync, as a separate content upsert.
  * Nodes without isFirstChild need only direct, so that is what sync will send.
* I had Claude do this, thinking it appropriate while working on <issue id="2565264d-8db7-4380-97b8-aad006e7e143" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2128/express-source-as-a-sourcedocument-slotreference-of-evidence">ENG-2128</issue>. It was decided that the testing would take too long, so it will be delayed. Still thinking it's worth examining the choices made while writing that code.
* Here are some decision points identified by Claude while doing this. Items marked "your design", "your call" or "you accepted" are Marc-Antoine's decisions; the others are Claude's choices.
  * Investigation — why schema updates never landed
    * Two independent sync paths, disagreeing: publishNodesToGroups used the cross-app converters but only inserted schemas missing from my_concepts; syncDgNodesToSupabase re-upserted schemas but through converters that emitted no slots and put template content under the template key that Obsidian reads as a template name.
    * The server was never the constraint — upsert_concepts already does ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE. Both gaps were client-side.
    * nodeTypeSince misses child-block edits (it tests :edit/time on the type block, while format lives in a child). Still unfixed; it means schema changes reach the DB mainly via sharedNodeTypeIds.

    sync-should-use-CrossApp
    * Concept names preserved for block-backed nodes ("{page title} {block text}") — otherwise every such concept would be renamed against a unique (space_id, name) index.
    * Variant became a property of the content, not of the slot it sits in — your design. That let the direct slot host a direct_and_description.
    * Missing first child → plain direct — your call.
    * The two-phase sync collapsed into one — your call, and it retired the withContents flag I'd added as a workaround. You read that flag correctly as a symptom.
    * Embeddings only for changed nodes — a node present solely for a full-content backfill hasn't changed and keeps its own.
    * CONCEPT_BATCH_SIZE 200 → 50, since concepts now carry full page markdown.
    * slot → defaultVariant — my rename collided with Concept.slots.
    * RoamFullContentNode removed, and times declared number (option A) rather than widened to string | number — number is both narrower and true, since all three producers are datalog rows.
    * Telemetry attribution shifts — markdown building moved into the getSharedFullContentUpdates phase; you accepted that.

    Deferred, deliberately
    * nodeTypeSince's blindness to child-block edits.
    * A published isFirstChild node sending both a direct_and_description and a plain direct (recorded as a comment in roamToCrossAppConverters.ts).
    * Producers returning CrossAppNode directly, together with folding node-type content into schema concepts — they share the upsertNodeSchemaToContent seam.
* History:
  * 2026-07-15 meeting: Michael wrote that callers move to the CrossApp contracts only "until such time as the linear task says to update the caller to use `CrossApp` contract". [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/7iirRHpUd>)
  * 2026-07-22 meeting: Michael: "keep all roam to cross app converters in a single file". [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Ic0cf7vkT>)
  * 2026-08-04 meeting: Michael wrote that client functions convert "from roam/obsidian data > CrossApp\* contracts", and "this is BEFORE the post-converter eg CrossApp\* > Database". [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/9ib7OQWB7>) [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/I6XUbC8j7>)
  * 2026-08-23: Marc-Antoine created this ticket and draft PR <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> while working on <issue id="2565264d-8db7-4380-97b8-aad006e7e143" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2128/express-source-as-a-sourcedocument-slotreference-of-evidence">ENG-2128</issue>.
  * 2026-08-24 dev meeting: Marc-Antoine listed it, with <issue id="d1d8aa4e-e2ff-40f2-94c2-a6a8b36c2189" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2166/make-upsertconcepts-more-like-a-patch-than-put">ENG-2166</issue>, under <issue id="99bbd340-1a9c-43d7-8251-0fecde588a34" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2129/populate-reference-content-from-crossappnode-and-roles-from">ENG-2129</issue>'s "Lots of Claude discussion, generated many tentative…" note. [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/HYZ2jUfQB>)
  * 2026-08-28: Michael: "This is a draft PR to look at the entirety of the scope. This is not intended to be merged as is and will be broken down into smaller tickets."
  * 2026-10-09, Sid and Michael's meeting: Michael wrote that these tickets "need to be reconsidered" after v0: "should we move this into backlog? should a different strategy be proposed?" {"id":"ENG-2166","uuid":"d1d8aa4e-e2ff-40f2-94c2-a6a8b36c2189","title":"Make upsertConcepts more like a PATCH than PUT","description":"## Problem

* When data is absent in an `upsert_concepts` call, existing database data is overwritten.
  * The function applies defaults before reading the input, so it can't tell a missing field from an empty one.
  * As a consequence, every code path that writes a Concept has to agree fully on what it sends.
  * This was identified while comparing the Roam sync and publish paths.
* Nobody has reproduced a lost field yet.

## Solution

* Make `upsert_concepts` aware of missing fields, so it acts more like a PATCH than a PUT.

**Open decisions**

1. Do we need this at all? If Roam sync and publish share one conversion path (<issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>, <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>), they can't disagree, and the cause goes away.
2. Which fields? (Was "TODO: List specific fields.")
3. `reference_content`: Roam sync leaves out `local_reference_content` when a node has no Source (`conceptConversion.ts`). If a missing value keeps the stored one, removing a Source from an Evidence no longer clears it in the database. Callers would have to send `{}` explicitly.
4. `schema_id`: Marc-Antoine's asset-references spec proposes refusing a node whose schema can't be resolved. The draft in PR <pull-request id="6bc42125-20df-4cdb-99e1-170065516b25" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2166-upsertconcepts-overwrites-too-aggressively-325d25f14ff9">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1334</pull-request> keeps the stored schema instead. Decide the two together.

## Done When

* `upsert_concepts` does not clobber absent values.

## Out of Scope

* Changes to callers of `upsert_concepts`. Decision 3 may need one.

## Notes

* Right now, we treat reference_content and literal_content as a unit; we could decide to also make it an update, and use null as a sentinel delete value.
* I had Claude do a first draft of this.
* Here is a list of decision points
  * Absent means preserve; explicit means clear. Defaults are applied before input in jsonb_populate_record, so absence was indistinguishable from empty by the time it reached the UPDATE.
  * '' clears a description — jsonb has '{}' for that, text has only NULL, so an empty string became the escape hatch.
  * author_id preserves on absent — your call: it should never legitimately be NULL.
  * schema_id is erased only by declaring is_schema: true — your rule, rather than plain preserve.
  * is_schema left alone — your call; making absence preserve there would shift semantics for every existing caller.
  * Verification by rolled-back transaction, with a control run against main's functions proving the tests weren't passing vacuously.
* PR <pull-request id="6bc42125-20df-4cdb-99e1-170065516b25" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2166-upsertconcepts-overwrites-too-aggressively-325d25f14ff9">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1334</pull-request> (draft) holds the first draft. It changes `schemas/concept.sql` and `addConcepts.feature`, has no migration yet, and has no reviews.

  * 2026-08-23: Marc-Antoine created this and PR <pull-request id="6bc42125-20df-4cdb-99e1-170065516b25" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2166-upsertconcepts-overwrites-too-aggressively-325d25f14ff9">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1334</pull-request>.

{"id":"ENG-1794","uuid":"b2336c31-b4ea-4e9a-886f-cf8e81c55e6a","title":"Atomic upsert of Concept and Content","description":"## Problem

We upsert Content and Concept separately; we can end up in situations where the latter upsert fails, and there is a discrepancy.

## Solution

Create a combined "upsert_resource" function, which would essentially handle a Concept and a list of Contents within the concepts. (A list because we want to handle, eg. direct and full variant separately.) This can fail atomically.

**Status (2026-10-16)**

* The database half shipped: `upsert_concepts` accepts embedded Content since <issue id="b66b4d29-6edc-4fbe-bbbc-4cfaab6f9834" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1822/modify-upsert-concepts-so-it-accepts-embedded-content">ENG-1822</issue>.
* Roam publish already uses the single call.
* Roam sync (<issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>) and Obsidian sync (<issue id="9969e706-c4c9-4405-ad9e-70f888d270b9" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1823/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-obsidian">ENG-1823</issue>) still call `upsert_content` separately. Both wait on <issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue> to decide whether they go through the upsert route.

## Done When

* ~~We have created and tested this function.~~ Done in <issue id="b66b4d29-6edc-4fbe-bbbc-4cfaab6f9834" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1822/modify-upsert-concepts-so-it-accepts-embedded-content">ENG-1822</issue>.
* We use it in Roam and Obsidian instead of the separate functions.

(Those are probably subtasks.) They are <issue id="9969e706-c4c9-4405-ad9e-70f888d270b9" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1823/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-obsidian">ENG-1823</issue> and <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>.

## Out of Scope

## Notes

This is less urgent now that we have recovery functions, but I think it would avoid the issue developing again. Statistics from the previous task:

Currently, we have 23335 distinct Content and 20582 corresponding Concepts, so 2753 are missing.

(Actually 23671 Content rows, but that's because each Obsidian node gets two rows for title and content.)

* These counts are from 2026-05-24 and haven't been measured again.
* History:
  * 2026-05-24: Marc-Antoine created this.
  * 2026-06-01: Marc-Antoine started <issue id="b66b4d29-6edc-4fbe-bbbc-4cfaab6f9834" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1822/modify-upsert-concepts-so-it-accepts-embedded-content">ENG-1822</issue> as the first part. [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/tzKwV7plF>)
  * 2026-07-06: Michael: "Postponed until after v0 of Push and pull nodes between Roam and Obsidian." <project id="42055007-b7e8-47c3-95a1-8929908034b6" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/post-v0-roam-obsidian-sync-architecture-1e0070a3bac6">Post-V0 Roam–Obsidian sync architecture</project>, the post-v0 project, started on 2026-10-09.
  * 2026-07-17 meeting: agreed that <issue id="9969e706-c4c9-4405-ad9e-70f888d270b9" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1823/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-obsidian">ENG-1823</issue> and <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue> use the upsert route. {"id":"ENG-2061","uuid":"17320a42-9f07-49ff-bc23-ba9586e335bf","title":"Refactor `RoamFullContentNode` to use `CrossAppNode` contract","description":"## Problem

* `RoamFullContentNode` and `CrossAppNode` describe the same node. Michael: "It is basically the same type, different name" ([type](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-740e5638ca02078f61f320b8654a1a5b2cad3350046a466abd1f8bf556c95b95L11>)).
  * `RoamFullContentNode` (`convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts`) is a flat datalog row: snake_case fields, times typed `string | number`, and `text`, `format` and `node_title`.
  * `CrossAppNode` is nested, with `content.direct` and `content.full`.
* Michael: "This likely removes the need for this converter" ([converter](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-3369b2954fe17df153f37f163d9fb033a7afd3063bf9e77142aed5ff214e805aR5>)). The converter, `fullContentNodeToCrossApp` (`roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`), derives `coreTitle` from the title format and builds the full content. That work moves; it doesn't go away.

## Solution

* Remove `RoamFullContentNode`. <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>'s Done When includes this ticket.

**Open decisions**

1. Is this the first sub-ticket of <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>, part of <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>'s single change, or closed because `RoamFullContentNode` is a fair input row type?
2. Does the full-content producer, `getSharedRoamNodesWithFullContentUpdatesSince`, return `CrossAppNode` directly? <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> removed the type but deferred "Producers returning CrossAppNode directly".
3. Does this ticket also cover `RoamDiscourseNodeData` (`getAllDiscourseNodesSince.ts`), the row type the direct-content path uses? No ticket covers it.

## Done When

* `RoamFullContentNode` is gone from the Roam codebase, including tests.

## Out of Scope

* Changing the sync write calls (<issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>).

## Notes

* Current state: the type is used in `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`, `roamToCrossAppConverters.ts` and `__tests__/syncSharedNodeAssets.test.ts`. PR <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> deletes `convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts` and types the times as `number`.
* History:
  * 2026-07-22 meeting: Marc-Antoine: "Suggestion: A converter for each roam-based type to CrossAppType, in a separate file."   * 2026-07-22: Marc-Antoine on <pull-request id="621db41e-f6ed-4815-aedf-03a62aeb818d" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2059-refactor-existing-roam-to-crossapp-converter-into-its-own-79ae73b79c6a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1243</pull-request>: "Rather than add a parameter to the converter, I thought I could add the full text here, as it feels natural for the type." [PR comment](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243#discussion_r3634076032>)
  * 2026-07-23: Michael created this ticket from <pull-request id="621db41e-f6ed-4815-aedf-03a62aeb818d" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2059-refactor-existing-roam-to-crossapp-converter-into-its-own-79ae73b79c6a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1243</pull-request> (<issue id="9d9d3eab-8868-493a-bc45-6d1b5e0df244" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2059/refactor-existing-roam-to-crossapp-converter-into-its-own-file">ENG-2059</issue>), 20 minutes before it merged.

{"id":"ENG-1824","uuid":"dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f","title":"Use the unified upsert_concepts in Roam","description":"## Problem

* Roam sync writes Concepts and Content in separate calls, to `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content`. If one call fails, we have partially defined nodes in the database.
* It would be better to send the full node, with Content as sub-objects of the Concept, in a single upsert. `upsert_concepts` accepts this since <issue id="b66b4d29-6edc-4fbe-bbbc-4cfaab6f9834" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1822/modify-upsert-concepts-so-it-accepts-embedded-content">ENG-1822</issue>.
* Roam publish already writes in a single call. Roam sync does not.

## Solution

* Remove the calls to `upsert_content`. Unify the Content computations to create the CrossAppNode type, and send it, after conversion, in a single call.

**Open decisions**

1. Does the single call go through the upsert route (<issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue>) or straight to `upsert_concepts`? On 2026-07-17 we agreed on the route. <issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue> has to confirm that still holds after v0.
2. <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue> (Roam sync onto the CrossApp converters) is the same work. Is it a step of this ticket, or does it replace this ticket? <issue id="b90793f4-5dc0-40fc-9942-95895531ba24" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2413/decide-how-roam-and-obsidian-move-onto-the-crossapp-types">ENG-2413</issue> decides this.
3. If we use the route, does this ticket also move Roam publish to it? Publish calls `upsert_concepts` directly today, and no ticket covers moving it.

## Done When

* There is no `upsert_content` call left in the Roam codebase, including test harnesses.

## Out of Scope

## Notes

* Today's `upsert_content` calls: `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts` (two calls) and `upsertNodesAsContentWithEmbeddings.ts`. Test harnesses: `fileReferenceHarness.ts` and `syncSharedNodeAssets.test.ts`.

  * 2026-05-30: Marc-Antoine created this as the Roam half of <issue id="b2336c31-b4ea-4e9a-886f-cf8e81c55e6a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1794/atomic-upsert-of-concept-and-content">ENG-1794</issue>.
  * 2026-06-25: Marc-Antoine: "Best done after <issue id="585c1ffc-4a96-443d-81a7-ced2414a7b58" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-892/add-roam-full-markdown-content-variant-for-shared-nodes">ENG-1848</issue>" (now <issue id="585c1ffc-4a96-443d-81a7-ced2414a7b58" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-892/add-roam-full-markdown-content-variant-for-shared-nodes">FEE-892</issue>).
  * 2026-07-17 meeting: agreed to change this ticket to use the upsert route. {"id":"ENG-2165","uuid":"8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea","title":"Refactor Roam Sync to use crossAppNodes","description":"## Problem

* We have two paths to write to the database: sync and publish. They use different converters, which violates DRY.
  * Sync converts with `discourseNodeSchemaToLocalConcept`, `discourseNodeBlockToLocalConcept`, `convertRoamNodeToLocalContent` and `convertRoamNodeToFullContent`. It writes with `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content` (`syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`).
  * Publish converts with `crossAppNodeToDbConcept` and writes with `upsert_concepts` (`publishNodesToGroups.ts`).
* We want the sync to use the same CrossApp converters as publish.

## Solution

* Large-scale: Rewrite the sync to use the publish converters.
  * To be broken down in sub-tasks
* PR <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> is not code I think we should check in as-is, but Claude-generated code which I sent to help us understand the scope and surface.

**Open decisions**

1. Is this ticket a step of <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>, or does it replace <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>?
   * As a step, this ticket moves sync onto the Roam-to-CrossApp converters and keeps the current write calls. <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue> then makes the single write.
   * This answers <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>'s Open decision 2.
2. Which smaller tickets does <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> split into, and in what order? Michael asked for the split on 2026-08-28.
3. Do the items <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> deferred get their own tickets? They are `nodeTypeSince` missing child-block edits, and published isFirstChild nodes needing both a `direct_and_description` and a `direct` Content.

## Done When

* The old sync path using RoamFullContentNode is removed.
  * This will include <issue id="17320a42-9f07-49ff-bc23-ba9586e335bf" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2061/refactor-roamfullcontentnode-to-use-crossappnode-contract">ENG-2061</issue>
* The sync path only upserts Concepts, with embedded Content, vs the two phases we have now.
  * <issue id="b2336c31-b4ea-4e9a-886f-cf8e81c55e6a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1794/atomic-upsert-of-concept-and-content">ENG-1794</issue>
  * <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue> has the same Done When. Open decision 1 decides which ticket owns it.

## Out of Scope

{"id":"ENG-2166","uuid":"d1d8aa4e-e2ff-40f2-94c2-a6a8b36c2189","title":"Make upsertConcepts more like a PATCH than PUT","description":"## Problem

* When data is absent in an `upsert_concepts` call, existing database data is overwritten.
  * The function applies defaults before reading the input, so it can't tell a missing field from an empty one.
  * As a consequence, every code path that writes a Concept has to agree fully on what it sends.
  * This was identified while comparing the Roam sync and publish paths.
* Nobody has reproduced a lost field yet.

## Solution

* Make `upsert_concepts` aware of missing fields, so it acts more like a PATCH than a PUT.

**Open decisions**

1. Do we need this at all? If Roam sync and publish share one conversion path (<issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>, <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>), they can't disagree, and the cause goes away.
2. Which fields? (Was "TODO: List specific fields.")
3. `reference_content`: Roam sync leaves out `local_reference_content` when a node has no Source (`conceptConversion.ts`). If a missing value keeps the stored one, removing a Source from an Evidence no longer clears it in the database. Callers would have to send `{}` explicitly.
4. `schema_id`: Marc-Antoine's asset-references spec proposes refusing a node whose schema can't be resolved. The draft in PR <pull-request id="6bc42125-20df-4cdb-99e1-170065516b25" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2166-upsertconcepts-overwrites-too-aggressively-325d25f14ff9">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1334</pull-request> keeps the stored schema instead. Decide the two together.

## Done When

* `upsert_concepts` does not clobber absent values.

## Out of Scope

* Changes to callers of `upsert_concepts`. Decision 3 may need one.

## Notes

* Right now, we treat reference_content and literal_content as a unit; we could decide to also make it an update, and use null as a sentinel delete value.
* I had Claude do a first draft of this.
* Here is a list of decision points
  * Absent means preserve; explicit means clear. Defaults are applied before input in jsonb_populate_record, so absence was indistinguishable from empty by the time it reached the UPDATE.
  * '' clears a description — jsonb has '{}' for that, text has only NULL, so an empty string became the escape hatch.
  * author_id preserves on absent — your call: it should never legitimately be NULL.
  * schema_id is erased only by declaring is_schema: true — your rule, rather than plain preserve.
  * is_schema left alone — your call; making absence preserve there would shift semantics for every existing caller.
  * Verification by rolled-back transaction, with a control run against main's functions proving the tests weren't passing vacuously.
* PR <pull-request id="6bc42125-20df-4cdb-99e1-170065516b25" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2166-upsertconcepts-overwrites-too-aggressively-325d25f14ff9">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1334</pull-request> (draft) holds the first draft. It changes `schemas/concept.sql` and `addConcepts.feature`, has no migration yet, and has no reviews.

Then I need to post the six comments across ENG-2091, ENG-1985, ENG-2045, ENG-2166, ENG-1823, and ENG-2165, matching the established writing style: direct, short sentences, bullets, no em dashes, consistent terminology, specific verbs. Before finalizing, I want to verify the facts in each comment—starting with ENG-2091, checking Marc-Antoine's rejection date, the relation discovery code paths, the converter's rid-setting behavior, the file locations and line numbers involved, and the frontmatter field used for importedFromRid.

Thinking through importedFromRid more carefully: for node types it actually lives in plugin settings (data.json) rather than frontmatter, while for notes and relations it's in frontmatter or relation data respectively. I want to phrase this simply as a field Obsidian keeps locally across notes, node types, and relations, without getting into the storage mechanics. I also want to note that Marc-Antoine's ideas about storing importedFromRid in the database are a separate design question for later, not part of this ticket—consistent with sid's "not binding" comment.

For ENG-1985, I'm confirming the details: Marc-Antoine's October 24 suggestion to refactor SharedNode into db code, the buildSharedNodes function in sharedNodes.ts, and the discovery logic that skips rows missing a schema, space, direct content text, or timestamp. I'm also noting that nodes without an author are currently kept as-is.

I'm verifying the local/remote id slots work correctly—local id for the same space, rid for the other space, matched via nodeRidById.

For ENG-2045, I'm checking that resolveImportedNodeContent correctly reads the file path from metadata, and that the import dialog pulls author names from the database account id as specified in the ticket.

For ENG-2166, I'm tracing through the conceptConversion and crossAppConverters files across Roam and Obsidian to confirm the described behavior matches the code on origin/main. I'm also working through the upsert_concepts logic to verify that an explicit empty value and a missing value produce the same stored result under current PUT semantics—tracing through the coalesce logic for reference_content step by step to confirm both paths land on an empty object, and starting the same check for the description field.

For description specifically, I notice a subtlety: under today's PUT, an empty string stores as '', not NULL, which isn't technically the same value even if readers likely treat them as equivalent. I decide to phrase my explanation carefully—noting that the reference_content case is safe on its own, while description needs a separate note that PR #1334 only clears it when the value is an empty string. I also want to flag the design risk where Publish omits the Source when it isn't yet present in the space.

Checking ENG-1823: Roam validates row ids while Obsidian only checks the call error, and Roam batches in groups of 200—both confirmed against sid's comment with line references. For ENG-2165, ENG-2061 and ENG-1824 are now sub-issues with the blocking relationship set correctly, and ENG-2166 won't auto-close when this lands. I decide to skip posting about ENG-1824 moving on ENG-1794, and note that the "Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25)" comments are posted under sid's API key and appear as "siddharth yadav."

AGENTS.md's rule about agent-created tickets doesn't apply since I'm not creating any new ones. Now I'm ready to write and post the comments—running the two structural redo calls alongside the six comments in parallel since they're independent of each other.

Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25): `CrossAppNode` follows the pattern of the other CrossApp types and gains no space or listing fields. This replaces the field list in the 2026-10-22 Decision comment and the Solution's "Add the missing fields to CrossAppNodes", after Marc-Antoine's -1 (2026-10-23).

The schema and relation converters already work this way. Each object carries a `rid`, local ids and the author's local id. Roam relation discovery looks spaces up separately with `getSpaceMap` (`discoverSharedRelations.ts:81`).

Each field a caller reads from `SharedNode` today moves like this:

- `spaceId`, `spaceName`, `spaceUri`, `platform`: discovery returns the spaces next to the nodes. A caller finds a node's space from the space in its `rid`. The converter sets `rid` on every node.
- `schemaId`: callers resolve the node type by the schema's rid (the node's space and `nodeType`), as relation discovery does with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp`.
- `authorId`: `CrossAppNode.authorId` is the author's account local id. Callers look names up by it.
- `directMetadata`: dropped. Its only reader is Obsidian import, for `filePath`, and import reads `filePath` again with each node's content (`importNodes.ts:1767-1774`, `importedNodeContent.ts:51`).
- `title`, `created`, `lastModified`: `content.direct.value`, `createdAt` and `modifiedAt`. `modifiedAt` stays the latest time of the Concept, the direct Content and the full Content.

`importedFromRid` stays as it is today: a field Obsidian keeps locally on imported notes, node types and relations. Discovery doesn't read it. Storing it in the database (one source space or several for a schema) is a later design question, not part of this ticket.

PRs, in order:

1. ENG-1985 adds the database-to-`CrossAppNode` converter.
2. This ticket's first PR: discovery returns `CrossAppNode` and the spaces, and the Roam callers switch.
3. ENG-2045: Obsidian import switches.
4. This ticket's last PR: delete `SharedNode`.

Done When doesn't change: `SharedNode` is removed without loss of functionality.

Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25), following Marc-Antoine's 2026-10-24 reply:

- Build the converter by refactoring the row logic in `buildSharedNodes` (`sharedNodes.ts`), not as new code beside it. Discovery keeps its current output in this PR; ENG-2091 switches discovery to the converter.
- The converter works like the schema and relation converters. It sets `rid` on every node, sets `authorId` to the author's account local id, and gives each slot target as a local id, or as a rid when the target is in another space.
- Open decision 1 (rows the contract can't represent): the bulk converter skips each such row and logs it, the way discovery already skips rows with no schema, no space or no direct Content. This includes nodes with no author. Discovery keeps them today, but `CrossAppNode` requires `authorId`, so the PR states this change.
- `CrossAppNode` gains no fields. See ENG-2091's 2026-10-25 Decision comment.

Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25), answering the open decision: `CrossAppNode` doesn't carry the author's database account id. Its `authorId` is the account local id, and the import dialog looks author names up by it. See ENG-2091's 2026-10-25 Decision comment.

- The listing's `filePath` goes away. Import already reads `filePath` with each node's content (`resolveImportedNodeContent`, `importedNodeContent.ts:51`), so the value from discovery was only a fallback that read the same field.
- The space name and platform come from the spaces that discovery returns next to the nodes.
- This lands after ENG-2091's first PR, which adds the discovery function, and before its last PR, which deletes `SharedNode`.

Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25): we do this, for Marc-Antoine's reason (2026-10-23): PATCH lets clients and plugin versions change at their own pace. This replaces the 2026-10-22 Decision, so this ticket no longer closes when ENG-2165 lands. We review PR #1334 now.

One problem to settle in that review. Today, a caller that leaves `local_reference_content` out clears the stored references. With PR #1334, leaving it out keeps them.

- Example: Alice removes the Source from her Evidence and syncs. Sync sends the Evidence without a Source reference. With PR #1334, the database keeps the old Source, and Bob still sees it when he imports the Evidence.
- These callers leave the reference out when a node has none: Roam sync (`conceptConversion.ts:88`, `:120`), Obsidian sync (`conceptConversion.ts:193`) and the shared publish converter (`crossAppConverters.ts:92`, `:119`).
- `description` needs the same check. PR #1334 clears it only on `''`, and Obsidian sends it at `conceptConversion.ts:68`.

Order:

1. A separate PR changes those callers to send an explicit empty reference when a node has none. Under today's `upsert_concepts`, an explicit empty reference does the same as a missing one, so this PR is safe on its own. Roam publish keeps leaving the Source out when the Source isn't in the space yet, so PATCH keeps the stored reference in that case. This PR comes after ENG-1823 and ENG-1824, so it changes their new code once.
2. PR #1334 merges, with its migration, after the Roam and Obsidian releases that carry step 1.

Users who don't update their plugin still keep stale references after step 2. The review weighs that. Open decisions 2 and 4 are answered in the same review.

Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25): Done When gains the two items from the 2026-10-22 review comment.

- Obsidian sync checks the ids that `upsert_concepts` returns and treats a -1 or -2 id as a failed node, as Roam sync does. Today it checks only the call error, so after the single write a failed node would be dropped without notice.
- Obsidian sync sends the nodes in batches, as Roam sync does, because each node now carries its Content and embedding.

The description's open decisions were answered on 2026-10-22: the single call goes straight to `upsert_concepts`, and ENG-1986 is a separate, later ticket.

Update (Sid, 2026-10-25):

- ENG-2061 and ENG-1824 are now sub-issues of this ticket, and ENG-2061 blocks ENG-1824.
- ENG-2166 no longer closes when this lands. It goes ahead (see its 2026-10-25 Decision comment), and its caller change comes after ENG-1824.
- After ENG-1824, we compare the result with PR #1333 and write any remaining steps, or close this ticket if its Done When is met.

{"id":"ENG-2091","uuid":"e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09","title":"Unify SharedNode and CrossAppNode","description":"## Problem

* We have two types that represent an abstraction of a node, `SharedNode` (`packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts`) and `CrossAppNode` (`packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts`). This makes for a larger cognitive surface.
  * `SharedNode` is the discovery listing: what a user sees for the nodes in a shared space. It has no content body.
  * `CrossAppNode` is the write payload, with direct and full content.
* There are aspects of SharedNode that are missing from CrossAppNode:
  * ~~reference_content (missing)~~ Done: <issue id="99bbd340-1a9c-43d7-8251-0fecde588a34" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2129/populate-reference-content-from-crossappnode-and-roles-from">ENG-2129</issue> added `slots` to both types.
  * sourceId: unclear. `SharedNode.sourceLocalId` already maps to `CrossAppBase.localId`.
  * directMetadata: the direct Content row's `metadata`, not `literal_content`. Only Obsidian reads it, to get `filePath`.
  * Space and listing fields: `spaceId`, `spaceName`, `spaceUri`, `platform`, `schemaId` and the decorated `title`. Roam discovery and import use them.
* We have a lot of code that started using the SharedNode and will need refactoring: 8 files in `apps/roam/src`, and Obsidian's `getPublishedNodesForGroups` (`importNodes.ts`).

## Solution

* Add the missing fields to CrossAppNodes.
* Take the functions that create SharedNodes from database data, and create equivalent functions that create CrossAppNodes instead
  * No such function exists for nodes today. `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` covers schemas and relations only.
* Start using those new functions in the client code
* Remove SharedNodes

**Open decisions**

1. Does discovery return `CrossAppNode`, or do we keep `SharedNode` as a separate listing type? Michael (2026-07-22) and Marc-Antoine (2026-08-03) pointed to `CrossAppNode`. Sid (2026-07-20) described `SharedNode` as a lightweight listing.
2. If discovery returns `CrossAppNode`, do the space and listing fields go into `CrossAppNode`, or into a listing type that wraps it (for example `{ node, space, schemaDbId, directMetadata }`)?
3. What did "sourceId" mean?
   1. Equivalent to sourceLocalId
4. Which ticket builds the database-to-`CrossAppNode` function for nodes: this one or <issue id="0183af0a-6eb6-42b5-a4bd-67ce8d8ed38f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985/define-converters-between-database-schemas-and-cross-app-schemas">ENG-1985</issue>?
5. <issue id="fbc284c7-3cd5-45f8-af76-69797693d685" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2045/remove-obsidian-getpublishednodesforgroups-wrapper-consume-shared">ENG-2045</issue> moves Obsidian onto `SharedNode`. Does it wait for this ticket, or change its target?

## Done When

* We have removed SharedNodes without loss of functionality

## Out of Scope

* Adding functionality, adjacent refactors.

## Notes

* This ticket doesn't depend on the upsert route (<issue id="9153e532-2ad1-4043-b2e7-6ae4edf446f1" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2412/decide-the-upsert-path-for-roam-and-obsidian-writes">ENG-2412</issue>): discovery is a read path.
* History:
  * 2026-07-15 meeting: Michael: "create a task to update `CrossAppNode` and any callers to remove dbId". [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/sYQ9O9CJj>) <issue id="46fbb09e-4f2d-4a9b-9a3b-0de4b532ae9e" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2036/remove-ref-from-the-cross-app-node-contract">ENG-2036</issue> (<pull-request id="ce170656-7f6d-4c67-b32e-7a0d511bdc62" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2036-simplify-the-cross-app-node-contract-057a05658547">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1235</pull-request>) did this on 2026-07-16.
  * 2026-07-20: Michael on <pull-request id="8994f3ac-8118-41b4-8699-20066e9f5c9f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2019-extract-shared-cross-space-node-discovery-into-78b77fd1985a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1216</pull-request>: "Are we planning on re-using a CrossApp contract for the return type?" [PR comment](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3611773589>)
  * 2026-07-20: Sid replied: "CrossApp contract is for the setters and getters converters … SharedNode is a lightweight listing of what a user sees for the nodes that are in shared space." He planned the getters for <issue id="8d484b94-3f20-4341-866e-3b95315eaa90" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1856/store-source-identity-metadata-for-roam-imported-nodes">ENG-1856</issue>, which was released on 2026-07-27 without a node getter. [PR comment](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3613796080>)
  * 2026-07-22: Michael on <pull-request id="8994f3ac-8118-41b4-8699-20066e9f5c9f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2019-extract-shared-cross-space-node-discovery-into-78b77fd1985a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1216</pull-request>: "eventually should be CrossAppNode contract, but that can be defered to the next project". [PR comment](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3632617180>)

{"id":"ENG-2091","uuid":"e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09","title":"Unify SharedNode and CrossAppNode","description":"## Problem

* We have two types that represent an abstraction of a node, `SharedNode` (`packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts`) and `CrossAppNode` (`packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts`). This makes for a larger cognitive surface.
  * `SharedNode` is the discovery listing: what a user sees for the nodes in a shared space. It has no content body.
  * `CrossAppNode` is the write payload, with direct and full content.
* There are aspects of SharedNode that are missing from CrossAppNode:
  * ~~reference_content (missing)~~ Done: <issue id="99bbd340-1a9c-43d7-8251-0fecde588a34" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2129/populate-reference-content-from-crossappnode-and-roles-from">ENG-2129</issue> added `slots` to both types.
  * sourceId: unclear. `SharedNode.sourceLocalId` already maps to `CrossAppBase.localId`.
  * directMetadata: the direct Content row's `metadata`, not `literal_content`. Only Obsidian reads it, to get `filePath`.
  * Space and listing fields: `spaceId`, `spaceName`, `spaceUri`, `platform`, `schemaId` and the decorated `title`. Roam discovery and import use them.
* We have a lot of code that started using the SharedNode and will need refactoring: 8 files in `apps/roam/src`, and Obsidian's `getPublishedNodesForGroups` (`importNodes.ts`).

## Solution

* Add the missing fields to CrossAppNodes.
* Take the functions that create SharedNodes from database data, and create equivalent functions that create CrossAppNodes instead
  * No such function exists for nodes today. `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` covers schemas and relations only.
* Start using those new functions in the client code
* Remove SharedNodes

**Open decisions**

1. Does discovery return `CrossAppNode`, or do we keep `SharedNode` as a separate listing type? Michael (2026-07-22) and Marc-Antoine (2026-08-03) pointed to `CrossAppNode`. Sid (2026-07-20) described `SharedNode` as a lightweight listing.
2. If discovery returns `CrossAppNode`, do the space and listing fields go into `CrossAppNode`, or into a listing type that wraps it (for example `{ node, space, schemaDbId, directMetadata }`)?
3. What did "sourceId" mean?
   1. Equivalent to sourceLocalId
4. Which ticket builds the database-to-`CrossAppNode` function for nodes: this one or <issue id="0183af0a-6eb6-42b5-a4bd-67ce8d8ed38f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985/define-converters-between-database-schemas-and-cross-app-schemas">ENG-1985</issue>?
5. <issue id="fbc284c7-3cd5-45f8-af76-69797693d685" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2045/remove-obsidian-getpublishednodesforgroups-wrapper-consume-shared">ENG-2045</issue> moves Obsidian onto `SharedNode`. Does it wait for this ticket, or change its target?

## Done When

* We have removed SharedNodes without loss of functionality

## Out of Scope

* Adding functionality, adjacent refactors.

## Notes

* This ticket doesn't depend on the upsert route (<issue id="9153e532-2ad1-4043-b2e7-6ae4edf446f1" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2412/decide-the-upsert-path-for-roam-and-obsidian-writes">ENG-2412</issue>): discovery is a read path.
* History:
  * 2026-07-15 meeting: Michael: "create a task to update `CrossAppNode` and any callers to remove dbId". [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/sYQ9O9CJj>) <issue id="46fbb09e-4f2d-4a9b-9a3b-0de4b532ae9e" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2036/remove-ref-from-the-cross-app-node-contract">ENG-2036</issue> (<pull-request id="ce170656-7f6d-4c67-b32e-7a0d511bdc62" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2036-simplify-the-cross-app-node-contract-057a05658547">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1235</pull-request>) did this on 2026-07-16.
  * 2026-07-20: Michael on <pull-request id="8994f3ac-8118-41b4-8699-20066e9f5c9f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2019-extract-shared-cross-space-node-discovery-into-78b77fd1985a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1216</pull-request>: "Are we planning on re-using a CrossApp contract for the return type?" [PR comment](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3611773589>)
  * 2026-07-20: Sid replied: "CrossApp contract is for the setters and getters converters … SharedNode is a lightweight listing of what a user sees for the nodes that are in shared space." He planned the getters for <issue id="8d484b94-3f20-4341-866e-3b95315eaa90" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1856/store-source-identity-metadata-for-roam-imported-nodes">ENG-1856</issue>, which was released on 2026-07-27 without a node getter. [PR comment](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3613796080>)
  * 2026-07-22: Michael on <pull-request id="8994f3ac-8118-41b4-8699-20066e9f5c9f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2019-extract-shared-cross-space-node-discovery-into-78b77fd1985a">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1216</pull-request>: "eventually should be CrossAppNode contract, but that can be defered to the next project". [PR comment](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1216#discussion_r3632617180>)

{"id":"ENG-2091","uuid":"e17cf3a1-ece8-497e-a8b4-a44ea6b9be09","title":"Unify SharedNode and CrossAppNode","description":"## Problem

* We have two types that represent an abstraction of a node, `SharedNode` (`packages/database/src/lib/sharedNodes.ts`) and `CrossAppNode` (`packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts`). This makes for a larger cognitive surface.
  * `SharedNode` is the discovery listing: what a user sees for the nodes in a shared space. It has no content body.
  * `CrossAppNode` is the write payload, with direct and full content.
* There are aspects of SharedNode that are missing from CrossAppNode:
  * ~~reference_content (missing)~~ Done: <issue id="99bbd340-1a9c-43d7-8251-0fecde588a34" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2129/populate-reference-content-from-crossappnode-and-roles-from">ENG-2129</issue> added `slots` to both types.
  * sourceId: unclear. `SharedNode.sourceLocalId` already maps to `CrossAppBase.localId`.
  * directMetadata: the direct Content row's `metadata`, not `literal_content`. Only Obsidian reads it, to get `filePath`.
  * Space and listing fields: `spaceId`, `spaceName`, `spaceUri`, `platform`, `schemaId` and the decorated `title`. Roam discovery and import use them.
* We have a lot of code that started using the SharedNode and will need refactoring: 8 files in `apps/roam/src`, and Obsidian's `getPublishedNodesForGroups` (`importNodes.ts`).

## Solution

* Add the missing fields to CrossAppNodes.
* Take the functions that create SharedNodes from database data, and create equivalent functions that create CrossAppNodes instead
  * No such function exists for nodes today. `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` covers schemas and relations only.
* Start using those new functions in the client code
* Remove SharedNodes

**Open decisions**

1. Does discovery return `CrossAppNode`, or do we keep `SharedNode` as a separate listing type? Michael (2026-07-22) and Marc-Antoine (2026-08-03) pointed to `CrossAppNode`. Sid (2026-07-20) described `SharedNode` as a lightweight listing.
2. If discovery returns `CrossAppNode`, do the space and listing fields go into `CrossAppNode`, or into a listing type that wraps it (for example `{ node, space, schemaDbId, directMetadata }`)?
3. What did "sourceId" mean?
   1. Equivalent to sourceLocalId
4. Which ticket builds the database-to-`CrossAppNode` function for nodes: this one or <issue id="0183af0a-6eb6-42b5-a4bd-67ce8d8ed38f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1985/define-converters-between-database-schemas-and-cross-app-schemas">ENG-1985</issue>?

* We have removed SharedNodes without loss of functionality

* Adding functionality, adjacent refactors.

Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25), following Marc-Antoine's 2026-10-24 reply:

- Build the converter by refactoring the row logic in `buildSharedNodes` (`sharedNodes.ts`), not as new code beside it. Discovery keeps its current output in this PR; ENG-2091 switches discovery to the converter.
- The converter works like the schema and relation converters. It sets `rid` on every node, sets `authorId` to the author's account local id, and gives each slot target as a local id, or as a rid when the target is in another space.
- Open decision 1 (rows the contract can't represent): the bulk converter skips each such row and logs it, the way discovery already skips rows with no schema, no space or no direct Content. This includes nodes with no author. Discovery keeps them today, but `CrossAppNode` requires `authorId`, so the PR states this change.
- `CrossAppNode` gains no fields. See ENG-2091's 2026-10-25 Decision comment.

* Obsidian relation publishing is the reference behavior, but it needs validation against the cross-app relation contract.
* Any mismatch should be identified before Roam relies on the same relation shape.

## Solution

* Inspect existing Obsidian published relation schemas and relation instances.
* Validate labels, complements, roles, endpoint typing, stable identities, and endpoint bindings.
* Capture gaps as follow-up tickets rather than creating a new Obsidian relation export path.

## Done When

* Existing Obsidian relation export satisfies the <issue id="95486710-e3d2-4cac-ab42-5262ef52e6c4" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1863/define-cross-app-relation-contract-and-fixtures">ENG-1863</issue> contract or gaps are documented.
* Validation covers one relation schema and one relation instance with both endpoints shared.
* No new Obsidian relation transport format is introduced.

## Out of Scope

* Roam relation publishing or import.
* Obsidian relation importer changes.
* Relation acceptance UI.

## Notes

* Functional requirements: [F5: Relation schema and instance sharing](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/gs-lxH5H3>), [F9: Stable cross-app identity](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/914EWeU_9>).

{"id":"ad9d794f-8968-415f-bfb1-8358f6ab9f6f","body":"Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25): `CrossAppNode` follows the pattern of the other CrossApp types and gains no space or listing fields. This replaces the field list in the 2026-10-22 Decision comment and the Solution's "Add the missing fields to CrossAppNodes", after Marc-Antoine's -1 (2026-10-23).

The schema and relation converters already work this way. Each object carries a `rid`, local ids and the author's local id. Roam relation discovery looks spaces up separately with `getSpaceMap` (`discoverSharedRelations.ts:81`).

Each field a caller reads from `SharedNode` today moves like this:

- `spaceId`, `spaceName`, `spaceUri`, `platform`: discovery returns the spaces next to the nodes. A caller finds a node's space from the space in its `rid`. The converter sets `rid` on every node.
- `schemaId`: callers resolve the node type by the schema's rid (the node's space and `nodeType`), as relation discovery does with `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp`.
- `authorId`: `CrossAppNode.authorId` is the author's account local id. Callers look names up by it.
- `directMetadata`: dropped. Its only reader is Obsidian import, for `filePath`, and import reads `filePath` again with each node's content (`importNodes.ts:1767-1774`, `importedNodeContent.ts:51`).
- `title`, `created`, `lastModified`: `content.direct.value`, `createdAt` and `modifiedAt`. `modifiedAt` stays the latest time of the Concept, the direct Content and the full Content.

`importedFromRid` stays as it is today: a field Obsidian keeps locally on imported notes, node types and relations. Discovery doesn't read it. Storing it in the database (one source space or several for a schema) is a later design question, not part of this ticket.

PRs, in order:

1. ENG-1985 adds the database-to-`CrossAppNode` converter.
2. This ticket's first PR: discovery returns `CrossAppNode` and the spaces, and the Roam callers switch.
3. ENG-2045: Obsidian import switches.
4. This ticket's last PR: delete `SharedNode`.

Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25): we do this, for Marc-Antoine's reason (2026-10-23): PATCH lets clients and plugin versions change at their own pace. This replaces the 2026-10-22 Decision, so this ticket no longer closes when ENG-2165 lands. We review PR #1334 now.

One problem to settle in that review. Today, a caller that leaves `local_reference_content` out clears the stored references. With PR #1334, leaving it out keeps them.

- Example: Alice removes the Source from her Evidence and syncs. Sync sends the Evidence without a Source reference. With PR #1334, the database keeps the old Source, and Bob still sees it when he imports the Evidence.
- These callers leave the reference out when a node has none: Roam sync (`conceptConversion.ts:88`, `:120`), Obsidian sync (`conceptConversion.ts:193`) and the shared publish converter (`crossAppConverters.ts:92`, `:119`).
- `description` needs the same check. PR #1334 clears it only on `''`, and Obsidian sends it at `conceptConversion.ts:68`.

Order:

1. A separate PR changes those callers to send an explicit empty reference when a node has none. Under today's `upsert_concepts`, an explicit empty reference does the same as a missing one, so this PR is safe on its own. Roam publish keeps leaving the Source out when the Source isn't in the space yet, so PATCH keeps the stored reference in that case. This PR comes after ENG-1823 and ENG-1824, so it changes their new code once.
2. PR #1334 merges, with its migration, after the Roam and Obsidian releases that carry step 1.

Users who don't update their plugin still keep stale references after step 2. The review weighs that. Open decisions 2 and 4 are answered in the same review.

Decision (Sid, 2026-10-25): Done When gains the two items from the 2026-10-22 review comment.

- Obsidian sync checks the ids that `upsert_concepts` returns and treats a -1 or -2 id as a failed node, as Roam sync does. Today it checks only the call error, so after the single write a failed node would be dropped without notice.
- Obsidian sync sends the nodes in batches, as Roam sync does, because each node now carries its Content and embedding.

The description's open decisions were answered on 2026-10-22: the single call goes straight to `upsert_concepts`, and ENG-1986 is a separate, later ticket.
